newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine tax evasion $40 bln a year - congressman.
newsitem.headline: Argentine tax evasion $40 bln a year - congressman.

text.p: Tax evasion in Argentina totals $40 billion a year, which is more than 10 percent of gross domestic product, or equivalent to the annual budget, the Lower House of Congress' budget committee leader said.
But committee chairman Oscar Lamberto, a deputy for the ruling Peronist Party, said the situation had improved in recent years because more tax dodgers were in jail.

"We're not doing great, but we're much better off than two or three years ago, when there were 8,000 (evasion) cases in court and no arrests. Today there are less cases and more people detained for sums involving more than $1.0 million," Lamberto told local radio Tuesday.

In separate comments to newspapers, he said $21 billion in value added tax and $19 billion in income taxes were evaded yearly, a calculation he said was based on "what the Treasury should collect in revenue as related to annual GDP."
"Numbers show that tax evasion in Argentina ranks among the highest in the world," Lamberto said.

He favored lowering the VAT and employer payroll taxes to improve collection, and noted that without such high levels of tax evasion, "We wouldn't have a fiscal deficit or have to ask for foreign financing."
Argentina is expected to show a budget deficit of $5.0 billion this year, according to International Monetary Fund estimates.
